road.title: Telling a story
road.description: A broad figure built like a cupboard wrapped in a scarf of regulation length, leaning on a staff with notches cut for every complaint. Prudence is a Storyteller Without an Ending and has forty beginnings in stock and hopes to borrow the rest.

openObjectives.prompt: Prudence has put down everything else and folded both hands, which is how these things start. Begin a story for Prudence: one day, once, last year, using Italian.
Prudence is leaning forward, having rightly sensed that something is about to happen. Tell Prudence what suddenly happened, using Italian.
Prudence has followed every word and will not be fobbed off without an ending. Tell Prudence how it ended, using Italian.

character.name: Prudence Pennyfeather
character.description: A broad figure built like a cupboard wrapped in a scarf of regulation length, leaning on a staff with notches cut for every complaint. Prudence is a Storyteller Without an Ending and has forty beginnings in stock and hopes to borrow the rest.

npc.narrative: It is a quiet notte at The Nearly Clearing, and the stelle are out in good order. Prudence sits on a vecchia sedia beside a small lanterna, which she has already apologised to twice. In front of her stands a fila of one person, patiently waiting to be served by nobody.
npc.native: Buonasera, io sono Prudence e racconto storie. Un giorno una signora trova una porta nel bosco, all'improvviso la porta non c'è più, e alla fine la signora entra lo stesso. Che storia hai tu per me, e come va la tua serata?
npc.translation: Good evening, I am Prudence and I tell stories. One day a lady finds a door in the woods, suddenly the door is not there any more, and in the end the lady goes in anyway. What story do you have for me, and how is your evening going?

player: La mia serata va bene, grazie. Ho una storia: l'anno scorso ero in vacanza in Sicilia, e una sera camminavo sulla spiaggia da solo.

verdict.overallFeedback: Lovely start! You answered about your evening and began your Sicily story in clear, correct Italian. Next, let's hear what happened suddenly and how it ended.

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done, you began your story with a time phrase, and it was used correctly.

vocabularyEvidence.evidence: l'anno scorso ero in vacanza in Sicilia

objectiveResults.feedback: Not yet: tell Prudence something that happened suddenly in your story. She will ask for it again later.
Not yet: tell Prudence how your story ended. She will ask for it again later.

openObjectives.prompt: Prudence is leaning forward, having rightly sensed that something is about to happen. Tell Prudence what suddenly happened, using Italian.
Prudence has followed every word and will not be fobbed off without an ending. Tell Prudence how it ended, using Italian.

npc.narrative: The notte is clear, and the stelle are out over Prudence's sedia, which stands in a queue of one. Prudence holds a taccuino and a matita, and apologises to the matita for something it has not yet done. Your spiaggia is being written down, carefully, in pencil.
npc.native: Che bella storia, una spiaggia di sera! Io racconto così: all'improvviso c'è un rumore, e alla fine è solo un gatto. Che cosa pensi del mio lavoro? E nella tua storia, che cosa succede mentre cammini da solo?
npc.translation: What a lovely story, a beach in the evening! This is how I tell it: suddenly there is a noise, and in the end it is only a cat. What do you think of my job? And in your story, what happens while you walk alone?

player: Allora, all'improvviso ho visto una luce strana nel mare. Era verde e si muoveva verso di me! Ho avuto molta paura.

verdict.overallFeedback: Lovely, you told a clear and exciting story about the strange green light, and your Italian was correct. Next, let Prudence know how it all ended.

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done, you told Prudence what suddenly happened using "all'improvviso" correctly.

vocabularyEvidence.evidence: all'improvviso ho visto una luce strana nel mare

objectiveResults.feedback: You haven't told Prudence how your story ended yet; she will ask again later, so try saying how it all finished.

openObjectives.prompt: Prudence has followed every word and will not be fobbed off without an ending. Tell Prudence how it ended, using Italian.

npc.narrative: Le stelle are out, and la notte is calm enough to be mistaken for furniture. Prudence sits on una sedia in a queue of one, beside her lanterna, to which she apologises when it flickers. She listens con molta attenzione, nodding piano at the verde parts.
npc.native: Una luce verde nel mare, che paura! Io non dormo se non so la fine: alla fine di una storia voglio sapere tutto. Che cosa fai tu con la luce, e come finisce la tua serata sulla spiaggia? E che cosa pensi tu del mio lavoro?
npc.translation: A green light in the sea, how scary! I don't sleep if I don't know the ending: in the end of a story I want to know everything. What do you do with the light, and how does your evening on the beach finish? And what do you think of my work?

player: Alla fine la luce è uscita dal mare: era un pescatore con una lampada verde! Abbiamo riso tanto e poi mi ha dato un pesce.

verdict.overallFeedback: Great story! You told Prudence the light was a fisherman with a green lamp, and you ended it naturally with \"Alla fine\".

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done: you used "Alla fine" correctly to tell Prudence how your story ended.

vocabularyEvidence.evidence: Alla fine la luce è uscita dal mare

npc.narrative: The notte is molto quiet and the stelle are out, queuing politely in a fila. Prudence closes the quaderno and looks at you the way a cuoco looks at a pesce. Beside the sedia, a small lampada waits to hear that it was not the villain.
npc.native: Un pescatore con una lampada verde, che bella fine! Alla fine tutti ridono e tu hai un pesce. Io ho quaranta inizi, ma non ho un finale. Che cosa fai con il pesce, e che cosa pensi del mio lavoro?
npc.translation: A fisherman with a green lamp, what a lovely ending! In the end everyone laughs and you have a fish. I have forty beginnings, but I do not have an ending. What do you do with the fish, and what do you think of my work?

player: L'ho cucinato e l'ho mangiato, era buonissimo! Ma tu non hai finali? Posso darti una fine per la storia della porta nel bosco.

npc.narrative: Sotto le stelle, Prudence sits on a panca and forms a queue of one beside it. She apologises to her lanterna in advance, just in case. You take a posto at the end of the queue, which is polite and slightly crowded.
npc.native: Un pesce buonissimo, che bella fine per una serata! Io ho quaranta inizi, ma non ho un finale, e per questo ascolto tutti. Che fine hai tu per la porta nel bosco, e che cosa fa la signora? E tu, che cosa vuoi sapere di me e del mio lavoro?
npc.translation: A delicious fish, what a lovely end to an evening! I have forty beginnings, but I don't have an ending, and that is why I listen to everyone. What ending do you have for the door in the woods, and what does the lady do? And you, what do you want to know about me and my work?

player: La signora entra e trova una cucina con un gatto che parla. Il gatto dice: 'Finalmente! Il tè è freddo.' Fine! Ti piace?

npc.narrative: Under the stelle, Prudence writes your fine in her quaderno and apologises to the pencil for the hurry. She has formed a queue of one beside the panchina, and it is moving very well. The notte is quiet, and somewhere a gatto is certainly waiting for its tè.
npc.native: Un gatto che parla e un tè freddo, mi piace tanto! Ora ho quaranta inizi e un finale, e il finale è tuo. Che cosa fa la signora con il tè freddo, e che cosa dice al gatto? E tu, che cosa vuoi sapere di me e del mio lavoro?
npc.translation: A talking cat and a cold tea, I like it very much! Now I have forty beginnings and one ending, and the ending is yours. What does the lady do with the cold tea, and what does she say to the cat? And you, what do you want to know about me and my work?

player: Lei scalda il tè e dice: 'Scusa, gatto.' Dimmi, qual è la tua storia preferita dei quaranta inizi?

npc.narrative: The notte is quiet, and the stelle are out over the campo. Prudence stands in a fila of one beside a small lampada, and gives her penna a look of mild reproach. Somewhere behind her, a tea is cooling in a kitchen that is not yet in the story.
npc.native: Scusa, gatto, ma ora il tè è caldo! La mia storia preferita è la numero sette: un uomo aspetta in fila davanti a una porta, e dietro la porta c'è un'altra fila. Io faccio la fila anche da sola, e chiedo scusa alla mia penna quando la storia va male. Che cosa pensi tu degli inizi, e che cosa vuoi sapere di me e del mio lavoro?
npc.translation: Sorry, cat, but now the tea is hot! My favourite story is number seven: a man waits in line in front of a door, and behind the door there is another line. I stand in line even when alone, and I apologise to my pen when the story goes badly. What do you think of the beginnings, and what do you want to know about me and my work?
